messages:
lee: Cerulean Finance wants a 2-week POC. Requirements: isolated on-prem (no outbound), websocket stream preferred, function/tool calls to their internal risk gRPC, nightly CSV export to SFTP, SAML + customer KMS, and SOC2 artifacts. They asked for a one-page delta vs hosted and a tiny live demo. Any red flags?

maya: Clarify: 1) isolated = no control plane phone home? 2) CSV push vs pull? 3) load profile (p95 targets)?

lee: Answers: 1) no phone home, local control plane only. 2) we push nightly to their SFTP. 3) steady 8rps, spikes 60rps, p95 <350ms. Model family: quantized open model ok.

tony: Works but must ship offline control plane + model tarball. For toolcalls, run our adapter in their VPC that forwards to internal gRPC (no external calls). Recommend containerized adapter + systemd. For streaming, enable backpressure and small KV cache size on nodes.

maya: Quick demo snippet (stream + toolcall): ```python
from redwood import StreamingClient
client = StreamingClient(endpoint='wss://local-redwood:443', token='EPHEMERAL')
with client.stream(session_id='cerulean-demo') as s:
    s.send({"input":"check txn 42","tool_call":"risk_check"})
    for ev in s.recv():
        print(ev)
```

sec-bot: Security checklist: https://redwood.internal/security/onprem-checklist (internal). Need network diagram, KMS integration guide, and retention policy. Recommend ephemeral tokens (3-5m) backed by their HSM.

ops-bot: Ports doc: https://redwood.internal/infra/onprem-ports. Suggested ports: 443 (control plane), 50051 (adapter), 22/873 for SFTP where allowed.

tony: Ballpark presales quote: 2-week onprem POC license $25k one-time + model transfer $2k + eng support ~5 eng-days (~$8k). Adapter customization add ~2 eng-days ($3k). If they accept containerized adapter only, we can discount 15%.

maya: I'll assemble a one-pager + demo repo (stream + adapter stub) and a minimal network diagram template. Can deliver by tomorrow AM for kickoff this week.

lee: Great, please include a minimal curl demo we can run locally. Need it for their devs. :thumbsup:
